probes.why: Decides which packet W2-E is. CR15NetGame::Update enables the entire shipping spectator camera rig by itself, every frame, when (netgameFlags & 4) == 0 && CAM.SPECTATOR_TEAM_GATE(netGame) && *(u32*)netGame == 9 and no headset is worn -- both calls of that if/else live in one 20-byte window, registered as CAM.SPECTATOR_ENABLE_CALL_SITE. If the condition comes true on its own under -spectatorstream then free-fly, follow, level cameras, camera collision and the auto-director all turn themselves on and W2-E ships NO enable code; if it does not, W2-E writes one word. THE PROBE CALLS THE GATE ITSELF and reports its return value, so the answer is a measurement rather than a re-derivation of arithmetic already read out of the binary -- if my decode is wrong, the gate's own answer and the entrant table disagree and the disagreement is the finding. CORRECTION TO THE BRIEFED READ, and it is load-bearing: netGame+0x178 IS a 592-byte-stride per-entrant array (IDENT.PROFILE_JSON_OFF and IDENT.USER_ACTOR_GUID_OFF are both addressed as 592*index off it), but CAM.SPECTATOR_TEAM_GATE DOES NOT INDEX IT -- its bytes are 0F B7 81 78 01 00 00, ModRM 0x81 = mod 2, rm 1, no SIB, so base rcx + disp32 with NO index register. It samples ENTRANT 0, hard-coded. Indexing to the local user's slot would therefore measure a word the gate never reads, so this probe dumps the WHOLE table at USER.STRIDE spacing AND marks entry 0 as the gate's subject, which is what makes 'is the local user entrant 0' answerable from the artifact. That distinction decides whether W2-E writes the local user's team word or entrant 0's. It also reads netGame+0xDE as a WORD, because the gate's own first test is 66 83 B9 DE 00 00 00 00 -- a 16-bit compare; a u8 read of that field reports 0 for a word of 0x0100 and would say the gate is blocked when it passes. The launch command line is captured too, because how to read a lobbyTeam that is not 2 depends on whether this launch asked for -spectatorstream at all. Also closes W1-H section 9 item 2 (does the spectator component system have a local instance in a flat session) and item 5 (the ci+0x274 / ci+0x3C combination), by reporting the CS instance count, its local index and both CI flags. EXCLUSIVE because the question is whether the gate comes true ON ITS OWN: any probe in the same launch that writes camera, identity or team state would be measured as if it were the engine. It is otherwise a passive census and could share with read-only probes. GUARDS offline-bit-lock, and the declaration is backed by a MECHANISM rather than a justification. An earlier version of this field argued the lock was installed even when this probe loses the instance claim, because offlinelock::Apply() at bootstrap.cpp:340 precedes coexist::ClaimInstance at :401. THE LINE NUMBERS ARE RIGHT AND THE CONCLUSION WAS BACKWARDS: source order is not execution order. Apply() lives inside WorkerMain (defined :199); Attach (:391) calls ClaimInstance at :401 and RETURNS FALSE at :403 without ever reaching the CreateThread(WorkerMain) at :429. So a probe that loses the claim installs NO lock, which is the opposite of what was claimed and the worst shape a guard can take -- declared present, absent in fact, launch proceeding as if protected. The honest guarantee is therefore: this probe installs the lock ONLY when it wins the instance claim. Rather than promise that, the probe now READS offlinelock::Current().state -- which lives in shared memory precisely so a module that did not install the hook still reports what the hook observed, making it a statement about the PROCESS -- and FAILS with check offline-bit-lock-held if the process is not protected (Locked or AlreadyLockedInProcess). The declaration cannot outlive the thing it declares. Mutation-proved both ways offline: treating NotAttempted as held flips the check to ok, reverting flips it back to failed. ANSWERS, and each is a read this probe actually takes rather than one it volunteers to cover: netgame-identity-word is *(uint32_t*)netGame, reported raw and in hex; spectator-global-1420D3AE4 is RVA 0x20D3AE4 read through buildguard::MappedAddress, reported with the module base and the absolute address actually dereferenced, which is what that read asks for so a legitimate zero can be told apart from a read of the wrong address; clientinfo-3c is ci+SPECTATOR.CI_MODE_OFF off the local instance; and spectator-fixedclock-word is RVA 0x2099038 read TWICE, at attach and again after the match, because 'nobody writes it' is the claim under test and one reading cannot see a write in between. That last one is why w2e-freecam-wallclock-override is NOT parked as a separate read: it would have been a second row for the same global, and the architect's version specifies it better.
probes.scope: Establishes ONLY whether the engine's own enable condition holds in this session, and what the entrant team words are when it is evaluated. It does NOT establish that game+0x8560 propagates into netGame+0x178: it observes what the command line produced and never writes, because game+0x8560 is consumed by SESSION.BEGIN_MULTIPLAYER at session creation, so a write after state 9 would be too late to propagate and a negative would be measuring nothing. It does NOT establish that entrant 0 is the local user -- it dumps the table so that question is answerable, but answering it needs the slot-to-entrant map at netGame+0x138, which no packet has registered. A COULD-NOT-DETERMINE here means no match was reached or the build is not the measured echovr.exe; neither is a defect report. On the guard: a PASS from this probe means the process was verifiably protected by the offline-bit lock at the moment the verdict was written; a FAIL on offline-bit-lock-held means it was not, and the launch should be treated as unprotected regardless of what any descriptor declared. On spectator-fixedclock-word: this probe reports the flag at two moments and the value that would be substituted if it were non-zero; it does NOT establish that no writer exists, which is an image-wide claim no single run can settle. Zero at both readings is consistent with the design's assumption, not proof of it.
